The original Transformer applies **post‑normalization** after each sub‑layer (i.e., a normalization layer is placed after the residual addition in every Transformer block) [hnet p.8]. H‑Net notes that modern large language models use **pre‑normalization**: they place a normalization layer (e.g., RMSNorm) before the residual addition and typically add a final normalization layer after all residual blocks, rather than the post‑normalization design of the original Transformer [hnet p.8].

The original Transformer applies **post‑normalization** after each sub‑layer, i.e., a normalization layer is placed *after* the residual addition within each block. H‑Net notes that modern large language models use **pre‑normalization**: they place a final normalization layer (e.g., RMSNorm) *after* all residual blocks, before the next sub‑layer, to balance feature norms and signal propagation [hnet p.8].

The original Transformer applies **post‑normalization**: after each sub‑layer it adds a residual connection and then performs **layer normalization** [attention p.2].  

Modern large language models use a **pre‑normalization** convention, placing a normalization layer (e.g., RMSNorm) **before** the sub‑layer’s residual addition. H‑Net adopts this approach, adding an RMSNorm at the end of each network component to restore balance between processed features and residual signals [hnet p.8].
